item.title: Computing S(X) for Ruled Surfaces Defined by Stable Bundles on Curves of Genus 2
item.description: arXiv:2610.22573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper discusses the algebra of symmetric tensors for ruled surfaces defined by rank 2 stable vector bundles on curves of genus 2. The algebra is computed for special bundles $E$ when $S^2 E$ is destabilized by a line bundle and when $S^3 E$ is destabilized by a bundle of rank 2. A strategy for computation is discussed in regards to the other special bundles $E$. This paper also discusses the generalization of these strategies to higher genus and gives a computation when $E$ is not stable and may be written as a direct sum of line bundles.
item.dc:creator: Lillian McPherson

item.title: Generic vanishing for Dolbeault cohomology of mixed Hodge modules on abelian varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.22678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study generic vanishing for the Dolbeault cohomology of mixed Hodge modules, where the differentials in the Dolbeault complex are modified by a one-form. We prove that, on the Dolbeault moduli space of Higgs line bundles, the cohomology support loci of mixed Hodge modules agree with the images of the cohomology support loci of their underlying $\mathscr{D}$-modules on the de Rham moduli space under the map induced by the nonabelian Hodge correspondence. We further apply this result to study Fourier-Mukai transforms of mixed Hodge modules on abelian varieties. We show that the extended Fourier-Mukai transform for bounded complexes of mixed Hodge modules has cohomology sheaves that are flat over the twistor line of $\lambda$-connections. This also gives an extension of Fourier transform of mixed Hodge modules to a compactification of the de Rham moduli space.
item.dc:creator: Ze Yun

item.title: Vector bundles on singular surfaces and threefolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.22679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We fully classify vector bundles of critical rank on normal affine surfaces and threefolds over algebraically closed fields via their Chern classes. We also prove existence of rank $2$ bundles on threefolds with prescribed first and second motivic Chern classes. The main input is the motivic filtration on algebraic $K$-theory: its third piece is generated by smooth closed points and is identified with motivic cohomology by the third Chern class.
item.dc:creator: Jean Fasel, Maria Yakerson

item.title: Hypercube Richardson varieties from magic words
item.description: arXiv:2610.22730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by the recent preprint of Ellenberg, Libedinsky, Plaza, Simental, and Williamson, we study the geometry of Richardson varieties whose associated Bruhat intervals are boolean posets. We define magic words for a Bruhat interval and prove that for intervals with magic words the associated Richardson variety is a tower of $\mathbb{P}^1$-s. We also prove that the Bruhat intervals consisting of the dyadically well-distributed permutations all have magic words. This gives a new proof that they form a boolean poset.
item.dc:creator: Bal\'azs Elek

item.title: $a$-numbers of covers in characteristic two: semigroups and Riemann-Roch spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.22755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the $a$-numbers of the Garcia-G\"uneri-Stichtenoth curves, the Beelen-Montanucci curves, and the Skabelund covers of Suzuki curves in characteristic two. The proofs use the identity $a(X)=\ell(\tfrac12\operatorname{div}(dt))$ and reduce the calculations to Riemann-Roch spaces on the base curves. We obtain transfer formulas for odd-degree radical covers, with one or several points at infinity, and evaluate them using Weierstrass semigroups and plane sections of the Hermitian curve. For the first two families we also give cyclic models over the projective line and relate the formulas to Elkin's rank formula. We then treat two classes of Artin-Schreier fibre products. A supersingular genus-six family has a-number $3$ at the zero parameter and $2$ elsewhere, although the genera and $a$-numbers of its quadratic quotients remain fixed. We determine its Ekedahl--Oort types as $(0,0,0,1,2,3)$ and $(0,1,1,2,3,4)$,
item.dc:creator: Gilberto B. Almeida Filho, Saeed Tafazolian, St\'efani C. Vieira

item.title: $R$-trivial Galois cohomology classes and cohomological $p$-dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.22758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a prime $p$, a field $F$ of characteristic different from $p$ and a finite $p$-primary Galois module $V$, a Galois cohomology class in $H^n(F,V)$ is called $R$-trivial if it can be connected to $0$ by a class defined over an open subscheme of the projective line. All classes of $H^n(F,V)$ are $R$-trivial if $F$ has cohomological $p$-dimension at most $n$, by the Bloch-Kato conjecture. We show that this bound is sharp: working over fields of iterated Laurent series, we produce, for every $n\geq 1$, a field $F$ of cohomological $p$-dimension $n+1$ and a Galois module $V$ such that $H^n(F,V)$ contains classes which are not $R$-trivial. The module $V$ is a quotient of the permutation module on the affine hyperplanes of an elementary abelian $p$-group, arising as a quotient of the absolute Galois group of $F$. We also describe $R$-trivial classes as sums of corestrictions of cup products involving a Kummer class.
item.dc:creator: Charles De Clercq

item.title: Low-weight compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal M_{g,n}^{ct}$ and the extended Torelli morphism
item.description: arXiv:2610.22809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the weight zero and weight two graded pieces of the compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal M_{g,n}^{ct}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus $g$ of compact type and show that they are computed by bridgeless graph complexes. In weight two, we construct a natural embedding of shifted weight zero cohomology from lower genus. For unmarked curves, we construct canonical classes represented by pinched odd wheel graphs and prove that distinct wheel monomials give linearly independent classes in the dual of $W_0H_c^{2g}(\mathcal M_g^{ct};\mathbb Q)$. By relating the bridgeless graph complex to the $K$-theory of graphs and the Quillen spectral sequence, we show that these classes remain linearly independent after pushforward along the extended Torelli morphism $\mathcal M_g^{ct}\to\mathcal A_g$. Finally, we prove that the realizations of the motivic Lie algebra arising from $\mathcal M_g$ and $\mathcal A_g$ have the same image in the weight zero compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal M_g^{ct}$.
item.dc:creator: Amy Bradford

item.title: The geometric exceptional set for Fano threefolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.23024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the geometric exceptional set in Manin's conjecture for smooth Fano threefolds. We prove that every adjoint rigid surface with $a$-invariant one on a non-product smooth Fano threefold is normal. This yields a description of the geometric exceptional set in terms of the higher-$a$ locus, anticanonical conics, and del Pezzo fibrations. Zariski density arise only from the latter two contributions. For del Pezzo fibrations, we construct a finite collection of parameter covers which controlling the associated breaking maps. We classify their low-genus components for general smooth Fano threefolds yielding examples with potentially Zariski dense geometric exceptional sets in $22$ of the $105$ deformation families. Extending Batyrev-Tschinkel's example, we construct Fano fourfolds with quartic del Pezzo fibrations and an explicit Fano threefold with two degree-six del Pezzo fibrations, all with Zariski dense geometric exceptional sets. For this threefold, the original form of Manin's conjecture fails on every non-empty open subset for every anticanonical height.
item.dc:creator: Runxuan Gao

item.title: Seven ordered points and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.23227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the ordered GIT quotient of seven points on $\mathbb P^1$ with equal weights is not isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of any arithmetic complex ball quotient. Together with our companion paper and the known positive examples, this determines the equal weight case for every $n\ge6$: such a realization exists precisely for $n=6,8$. The lattice and the algebraic isomorphism are unrestricted, and torsion and divisorial ramification are allowed. The proof combines arithmetic reductions with identities involving Chern classes of fixed subvarieties and intersection inequalities for nef divisors on the GIT quotient. The final comparison includes all fixed components and requires no bound on the degree of an individual fixed curve.
item.dc:creator: Ryunosuke Nakano (Hokkaido University), Hisato Matsukawa (Hokkaido University)

item.title: Weighted configurations and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.23228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, for every $n\ge9$, no ordered GIT quotient of $n$ points on $\mathbb P^1$ with positive rational weights smaller than one and of total weight two is isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of an arithmetic complex ball quotient. The weights may lie on stability walls, and the lattice may have torsion and ramify along divisors. No compatibility with a prescribed period map is assumed. The proof compares homomorphisms from the tangent bundle to line bundles of negative degree with normal bundles of arithmetic fixed subvarieties. We describe these homomorphisms through coincident marked points and prove vanishing statements for their kernels. The comparison, together with integrality of Chern classes and the invariant theory of finite reflection groups, gives the nonexistence theorem without a Fano assumption on the GIT quotient.
item.dc:creator: Ryunosuke Nakano (Hokkaido University), Hisato Matsukawa (Hokkaido University)

item.title: Ambient Chow Rings of Debarre--Voisin Fourfolds and the Beauville--Voisin Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.23376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Beauville--Voisin conjecture for a very general Debarre--Voisin hyperk\"ahler fourfold \(Y\subset\Gr(6,10)\) associated with a trivector \(\sigma\) on a ten-dimensional complex vector space \(V_{10}\). Namely, the cycle class map is injective on the subalgebra of the Chow ring generated by divisor classes and the Chern classes of the tangent bundle.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Akazawa

item.title: Brauer-Manin obstruction for symmetric powers
item.description: arXiv:2610.23430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a quasi-projective smooth geometrically integral variety $X$ over a number field, we prove that the Brauer-Manin obstruction for its symmetric powers coincides with the obstruction coming from $X$. As a consequence, Brauer-Manin obstruction for the symmetric powers cannot provide new cohomological obstruction to weak approximation of zero-cycles for $X$. The key intermediate ingredients are a Dold-Thom type result for Brauer groups and a precise descent formula for adelic points.
item.dc:creator: Yang Cao, Lin Zhou

item.title: Smooth Limits of Stable Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.23457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let X be a compact complex manifold of dimension n, and suppose that X is deformation equivalent to a stable manifold. Then X is projective whenever n <=3. We also construct, for every n >=4, smooth families of compact complex manifolds over the unit disc such that every fiber over the punctured disc is a stable manifold, while the central fiber is a non-Kahler Moishezon manifold.
item.dc:creator: Mu-Lin Li

item.title: Lefschetz Pencils on surfaces and an application to Seshadri constants
item.description: arXiv:2610.23485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a nonsingular complex projective surface and let $L$ be a very ample line bundle on $X$. We study the question: when does a general pencil in the linear system $|L|$ consist of only irreducible and reduced curves? We give a precise condition which guarantees an affirmative answer: in fact, this holds if and only if the genus of a general member of $|L|$ exceeds the irregularity of $X$. The proof is topological, using vanishing cycles and the theory of Lefschetz pencils. As an application, combined with a construction due to Miranda, we prove that for any positive rational number $\delta$ there exist a blow up $Y \to X$ at finitely many points, an ample line bundle $M$ on $Y$ and a point $x \in Y$ such that $\varepsilon(Y,M,x) = \delta$; Miranda proved this when $X = \mathbb{P}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Krishna Hanumanthu, A. J. Parameswaran

item.title: mixed Hodge structures on the strictly upper triangular Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.23505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that, for $k\geq 3$, a lattice in the unitriangular Lie group $U_k(\mathbb{R})$ is the fundamental group of a smooth quasi-projective complex algebraic variety if and only if $k=3$. The proof uses the conjugation symmetry and weight conditions of mixed Hodge structure on the Malcev Lie algebra proven by Morgan. This result identifies a family of groups that must be excluded in the search for smooth quasi-projective varieties with torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups of high nilpotency class.
item.dc:creator: Taito Shimoji

item.title: On the crystalline Artin--Mumford invariant
item.description: arXiv:2610.23516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ and let $W=W(k)$. We prove that the torsion subgroup of $H^3_{\mathrm{cris}}(X/W)$ is a birational invariant of smooth projective varieties over $k$. The proof combines the action of correspondences on Hodge--Witt cohomology and on the first Nygaard piece of the de Rham--Witt complex.
item.dc:creator: Margherita Pagano, Domenico Valloni

item.title: Local topological zeta functions of generic symmetric and catalecticant determinantal varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.23689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give explicit formulas for the local topological zeta functions at the origin of generic symmetric determinantal varieties and catalecticant determinantal varieties associated with generic Hankel matrices. In the symmetric determinant hypersurface case, the formula simplifies to a closed product expression and implies the Strong Monodromy Conjecture. For catalecticant determinantal varieties, we establish a simultaneous local reduction of the determinantal ideals and obtain a closed product formula for their local topological zeta functions. Together with the known Bernstein-Sato polynomial of the Hankel determinant, this also implies the Strong Monodromy Conjecture in the square catalecticant determinant case. The method used in this paper also gives short proofs of Chen-Zuo/Docamposs formula in the generic determinantal case and Chen-Shi-Xu-Zuo's formula in the skew-symmetric case.
item.dc:creator: An Khuong Doan

item.title: Spectral networks, finite webs, and the $T_3$ cubic differential
item.description: arXiv:2610.23752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe spectral networks for cubic differentials on $\mathbf{P}^1$ with exactly three poles all of order two, following observations of Hollands-Neitzke. To do so, we give a precise definition and establish some basic properties of a class of finite webs (corresponding to BPS states in physics) in the cubic differential setting, including their non-vanishing central charge. Turning to the example, we prove that at rational angles the network is totally degenerate; the number of walls and Stokes regions is explicitly computed and depends on an arithmetic criterion. At all other angles, the spectral network is dense in the surface and contains no finite webs, as expected. Physically, this example corresponds to a fundamental building block for a large class of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ QFTs with gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(3)$.
item.dc:creator: Omar Kidwai, Guillaume Tahar

item.title: Deligne--Faltings Logarithmic Derived Geometry with a View towards Logarithmic GLSM
item.description: arXiv:2610.23803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many perfect obstruction theories and virtual cycles in enumerative geometry are shadows from derived geometry. In this paper, we give a general construction of reduced perfect obstruction theories arising from a geometric reduction of the derived stack $X$ with respect to a $(-1)$-shifted log function $w_\alpha$. Notably, this construction leads to a decomposition of the virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ into the reduced virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{red}}$ and a reduced boundary cycle $[\Delta_X]^\red$. Our construction is motivated by future applications to the moduli stack of UMD logarithmic R-maps in log GLSM \cite{CJR21}. Along the way, we develop logarithmic analogs of several constructions in derived geometry, in particular proving a logarithmic Lagrangian intersection theorem.
item.dc:creator: Felix Janda, Ruoxi Li

item.title: Twisted $\mathbb{A}^1$-degrees of Wronski maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.23816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Wronski map is a central object of study in osculating Schubert calculus, and has been the focus of much work in real algebraic geometry over the last few decades due to its remarkable reality properties. In this work, we study it over arbitrary fields through the lens of quadratically-enriched enumerative geometry. A basic obstruction is that the Wronski map is not oriented in general, so existing approaches do not apply directly. To that end, we introduce twisted $\mathbb{A}^1$-degrees of finite flat lci maps of schemes, which generalize ordinary $\mathbb{A}^1$-degrees by allowing us to twist an orientation by the equation of a divisor, and $\mathbb{A}^1$-chambers, which generalize the notion of connected component of a real manifold. We then show that a certain weighted count of the fibers of the Wronski map depends only on the action of the absolute Galois group of the base field on the roots of the Wronski polynomial. This unifies Eremenko and Gabrielov's work on real degrees of Wronski maps, Levinson and Purbhoo's work on the character orientation of the real Wronski map, and Brazelton's work on enriched degrees of Wronski maps into one framework.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Brazelton, Jake Levinson

item.title: Presentability of categories of localizations and analytic rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.22494v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that certain categories of Bousfield localizations are presentable and give explicit regular cardinals $\kappa$ for which they are $\kappa$-presentable. As an application, we show that the category of analytic rings in the sense of Clausen and Scholze is $(2^{\aleph_0})^+$-presentable.
item.dc:creator: Wern Juin Gabriel Ong, Gabriel Ribeiro

item.title: Semialgebraic ${C^m}$ solutions to a univariate system of linear inequalities with Nash forcing
item.dc:creator: Fushuai Jiang, Garving K. Luli

item.title: Approximation and extension theorems for normal affine toric varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.22926v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study approximation and extension problems for holomorphic maps from Stein spaces to normal affine toric varieties, continuing the work of L\"ark\"ang and L\'arusson. Normality allows us to obtain twisted factorizations for arbitrary holomorphic maps from factorial complex spaces, including degenerate maps. This yields approximation and extension theorems under weaker cohomological assumptions. We also prove a simultaneous approximation and extension theorem under an additional codimension condition on the inverse image of the singular locus and a cohomological condition on the union of the interpolation submanifold and the approximation set. Finally, an explicit example with target $\{w^2=uv\}\cong\mathbb{C}^2/\{\pm1\}$ shows that simultaneous approximation and extension can fail even when the relevant cohomological obstructions vanish. Thus normality alone does not recover the full approximation and interpolation property of Oka manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Uchimoto

item.title: A cubulation of the associahedron using a torus-equivariant degeneration of the brick variety
item.description: arXiv:2610.23004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe a mixed subdivision of the $(n-1)$-dimensional Loday associahedron into $(n-1)!$ maximal cells which are combinatorial cubes, and we show that the face poset of this subdivision is isomorphic to the face poset of the subdivision of the $1\times 2\times \dotsb \times (n-1)$ box into unit cubes. More generally, we describe mixed subdivisions of generalized associahedra into pieces which are Minkowski sums of Bruhat interval polytopes. Our subdivisions arise from a torus-equivariant embedded (in a product of flag varieties) degeneration of brick varieties into reduced unions of products of Richardson varieties. The subdivision of Loday's associahedron allows us to `embed' the 1-skeleton of the permutahedron in the boundary of the associahedron.
item.dc:creator: Raj Gandhi, Gabe Udell

item.title: Point Modules of Non-Connected Graded Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.23171v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As part of a program to extend the homogeneous coordinate ring techniques of Artin-Tate-Van den Bergh to twisted graded Calabi-Yau (tCY) algebras, we initiate the study of point modules of non-connected graded algebras. We define weak and strong point modules of graded quotients of path algebras and compute their respective moduli stacks. We describe the relation between these point stacks and the classical point schemes in the connected graded setting, and we analyze the point stacks of several 2 and 3-dimensional tCY algebras.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Lamkin

item.title: Folding to the Bessel-Clifford system, and Equivariant Topological Recursion
item.description: arXiv:2610.23320v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the interplay between symmetry reductions of meromorphic connections, folding, and topological recursion. As a motivating example, we realize the Bessel-Clifford system as a folding of a symmetry-invariant subspace of the $0-$member of the Painlev\'e IV hierarchy. We introduce equivariant topological recursion for spectral curves with a Klein four-group $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry and prove that the corresponding equivariant correlators can be folded to the ordinary topological recursion correlators on the quotient spectral curve. We further establish the compatibility of this folding with the associated wave functions and quantum curves. In the Bessel-Clifford example, this yields an explicit relation between the equivariant and folded wave functions and recovers the corresponding quantum curve reduction. These results provide a framework for relating symmetry reductions of integrable systems to folding operations in topological recursion.
item.dc:creator: Mohamad Alameddine, Alexander Hock

item.title: A Topological Quantum Field Theory for Representation Varieties of Torus Links
item.description: arXiv:2610.23644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT) that computes the virtual classes of $G$-representation varieties associated with the fundamental group of a torus link complement. Following the framework established by Gonz\'alez-Prieto, Logares and Mu\~noz for $G$-representation varieties of surface groups, we introduce a suitable bordism whose iteration enables a recursive topological evaluation of these virtual classes. Via this TQFT, we explicitly compute the virtual class of these varieties for the groups $G=\mathrm{AGL}_1(\mathbb{C})$ and $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$.
item.dc:creator: Enrique Aycart-Maldonado, Alejandro Calleja

item.title: Finite Cyclic Fundamental Groups and Exotic Universal Covers from the Cartwright--Steger Surface
item.description: arXiv:2610.23711v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use a particular nodal curve on the Cartwright-Steger surface to construct minimal symplectic four-manifolds with arbitrary nontrivial finite cyclic fundamental group and fixed topological invariants $(e,\sigma,\chi_h,c_1^2)=(43,1,11,89)$. Using these symplectic four-manifolds as building blocks, we construct a symplectic 4-manifold that is homeomorphic to $(22m-1)\mathbb{CP}^2\#(21m-1)\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}$ for any integer $m\geq 2$.
item.dc:creator: Anar Akhmedov, B. Doug Park, S\"{u}meyra Sakall{\i}, Sai-Kee Yeung

item.title: Dg models for derived differential operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.23778v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that for any algebra $R$ that is essentially of finite type over a field $k$, the derived functors of Smith-Van den Bergh admit a dg enhancement. In particular, for any $R$-module $M$ one can associate a dg algebra of differential operators $E_M$ whose cohomology is a nilpotent thickening of the (classical) ring of $k$-linear differential operators on $M$. We show that these dg algebras fit into a framework of Koszul duality due to Dwyer-Greenlees and specializes to a derived ring of differential operators studied by Yang when $M=R$ and $k=\mathbb{C}$. In particular, upon fixing a presentation $R=S/I$ with $S$ essentially smooth, we show a derived Kashiwara's equivalence, namely that whenever $\mathrm{supp}_S(M)=\mathrm{V}(I)$ then there is an equivalence of triangulated categories between the derived category of dg ${E}_M$-modules and the derived category of $D$-modules on $S$ that are set-theoretically supported on $I$. Finally, in the case of positive characteristic, we show that the dg algebra ${E}_M$ admits a description in terms of the Frobenius endomorphism akin to the classical description of differential operators, and the proof employs simplicial techniques to obtain a result of independent interest in commutative algebra.
item.dc:creator: Jack Jeffries, Devlin Mallory, Claudia Miller, Josh Pollitz, Eamon Quinlan-Gallego

item.title: Identifiability from Moments in Independent Component Analysis Mixture Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.23846v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Independent Component Analysis (ICA) mixture models. These models consist of mixtures of ICA densities. An ICA density is associated with a random vector whose coordinates become mutually independent after an invertible linear transformation. ICA mixture models are nonparametric extensions of the celebrated family of Gaussian mixtures. We show that in many cases the ICA mixtures are identifiable from the collection of the observed moment tensors, that is, the mixing coefficients, linear transformations, and source moments of order up to $d$ can be identified from the moment tensors of order up to $d$ for generic parameters. We address the problem by studying the corresponding secant varieties and their algebraic properties such as dimensions and Gauss maps. In particular, for $n$-variate distributions, we establish that generically and up to the trivial scaling and permutation symmetries, when $d\geq 5$, the parameters can be recovered uniquely for asymptotically up to $n^{d-2}/d!$ mixture components. For $d=3,4$, we show identifiability up to a finite equivalence class for asymptotically up to $n^{d-2}/d!$ and $0.5 n^{d-2}/d!$ components respectively, where for $d=4$ the mixing coefficients need to be known a priori. The obtained bounds on the component numbers have the maximum possible orders in $n$, and for $d = 3$ and $d\geq 5$, they are also asymptotically sharp.
item.dc:creator: Pardis Semnani, Konstantin Usevich, Elina Robeva

item.title: Normal complex surface singularities with rational homology disk smoothings
item.description: arXiv:1311.1929v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we show that if the minimal good resolution graph of a normal surface singularity contains at least two nodes (i.e. vertex with valency at least 3) then the singularity does not admit a smoothing with Milnor fiber having rational homology equal to the rational homology of the 4-disk $D^4$ (called a rational homology disk smoothing). Combining with earlier results, this theorem then provides a complete classification of resolution graphs of normal surface singularities with a rational homology disk smoothing, verifying a conjecture of J. Wahl regarding such singularities. Indeed, together with a recent result of J. Fowler we get the complete list of normal surface singularities which admit rational homology disk smoothings.
item.dc:creator: Heesang Park, Dongsoo Shin, Andr\'as I. Stipsicz

item.title: Singularities of orthogonal and symplectic determinantal varieties
item.description: arXiv:2311.07549v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let either $GL(E)\times SO(F)$ or $GL(E)\times Sp(F)$ act naturally on the space of matrices $E\otimes F$. There are only finitely many orbits, and the orbit closures are orthogonal and symplectic generalizations of determinantal varieties, which can be described similarly using rank conditions. In this paper, we study the singularities of these varieties and describe their defining equations. We prove that in the symplectic case, the orbit closures are normal with good filtrations, and in characteristic $0$ have rational singularities. In the orthogonal case we show that most orbit closures will have similar properties, and determine precisely the exceptions to this.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'as Cristian L\H{o}rincz

item.title: On the Hodge Structures of Global Smoothings of Normal Crossing Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2404.19229v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Hodge theory of smooth fibers of semistable degenerations of compact complex manifolds with central fibers of K\"ahler type. If every stratum of the central fiber is a $\partial\overline{\partial}$-manifold, we prove that the local invariant cycle property in all degrees implies that the nearby fibers satisfy the $\partial\overline{\partial}$-lemma. In middle degree, the corresponding property alone yields a canonical Hodge decomposition on the nearby fibers and an explicit formula, in terms of the limiting mixed Hodge structure, for the signature of the cup-product pairing on each Hodge component. This gives a partial converse to Clemens' local invariant cycle theorem for K\"ahler degenerations. As applications, we study global smoothings of ordinary double points and extend results of Friedman and Li on Clemens manifolds. We also apply our results to the non-K\"ahler Calabi--Yau manifolds constructed by Hashimoto--Sano and Sano. In particular, these manifolds satisfy the $\partial\overline{\partial}$-lemma, even though they are not in Fujiki class $\mathcal{C}$, and in Sano's higher-dimensional examples we explicitly determine the failure of the Hodge--Riemann bilinear relations on the middle cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Kuan-Wen Chen

item.title: Decorated trees
item.description: arXiv:2409.11559v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a class of combinatorial objects that we call "decorated trees". These consist of vertices, arrows and edges, where each edge is decorated by two integers (one near each of its endpoints), each arrow is decorated by an integer, and the decorations are required to satisfy certain conditions. The class of decorated trees includes different types of trees used in algebraic geometry, such as the Eisenbud and Neumann diagrams for links of singularities and the Neumann diagrams for links at infinity of algebraic plane curves. By purely combinatorial means, we recover some formulas that were previously understood to be "topological". In this way, we extend the generality of those formulas and show that they are in fact "combinatorial".
item.dc:creator: Pierrette Cassou-Nogu\`es, Daniel Daigle

item.title: Logarithmic Crystalline Representations
item.description: arXiv:2504.14246v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1989, Faltings proved the comparison theorem between \'etale cohomology and crystalline cohomology by studying Fontaine-Faltings modules and crystalline representations. In his paper, he mentioned these modules and representations can be extended to the logarithmic context, but without detail. This note aims to explicitly present the construction of logarithmic Fontaine-Faltings modules and logarithmic crystalline representations.
item.dc:creator: Zhenmou Liu, Jinbang Yang, Kang Zuo

item.title: Pencils of projective hypersurfaces, Griffiths heights and geometric invariant theory. II Hypersurfaces with semihomogeneous singularities
item.description: arXiv:2506.22126v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper establishes a formula for the stable Griffiths height of the middle-dimensional cohomology of a pencil of projective hypersurfaces $H$, with semihomogeneous singularities, over some smooth projective curve $C$. This formula appears as Theorem 5.1 in the first part of this paper (arxiv:2506.15334). The proof of this formula relies on the strategy developed in my previous work (arxiv:2212.11019v3) to derive an expression for this Griffiths height when the only singularities of the fibers of $H$ over $C$ are ordinary double points. To deal with general semihomogeneous singularities, we complement this strategy by the construction of a finite covering $C'$ of $C$ such that the pencil $H' = H \times_C C'$ over $C'$ admits a smooth model $\widetilde{H}'$ with semistable fibers with smooth components. This allows us to circumvent the delicate issue of the determination of the elementary exponents attached to the singular fibers of $H/C$.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mordant

item.title: Class field theory for function fields and finite abelian torsors
item.description: arXiv:2507.02483v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $U$ be a smooth and connected curve over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, with smooth compactification $X$. We generalize classical Geometric Class Field theory to provide a classification of fppf $G$-torsors over $U$ in terms of isogenies of generalized Jacobians, for any finite abelian group scheme $G$. We then apply this classification to give a novel description of the abelianized Nori fundamental group scheme of $U$ in terms of the Serre--Oort fundamental groups of generalized Jacobians of $X$; when $U=X$ is projective, we recover a well known description of the abelianized fundamental group scheme of $X$ as the projective limit of all torsion subgroup schemes of its Jacobian.
item.dc:creator: Bryden Cais, Shusuke Otabe

item.title: On the tangent bundle and the divisor theory of a general matroid
item.description: arXiv:2510.06609v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Extending classical algebro-geometric constructions to arbitrary matroids, we construct a $K$-class $T_M\in K(M)$ for every loopless matroid $M$. When $M$ is realizable by a linear subspace $L$, $T_M$ recovers the $K$-class of the tangent bundle of the wonderful compactification $W_L$. We derive two formulas for the total Chern class of $T_M$ (one combinatorial and one geometric) and show that the associated Todd class agrees with the Todd class appearing in the matroid Hirzebruch--Riemann--Roch formula. To develop a positivity theory entirely at the combinatorial level, we introduce the notion of a "fake effective cone", a combinatorial analogue of the classical effective cone, and use it to characterize big and nef divisors in $A(M)$. Finally, we define the $\beta_S$ classes, obtained from Cremona conjugates of the classical $\alpha_S$ classes, and study their properties to provide a rich and computable family of combinatorially nef divisors.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN, 2026, no. 17, rnag188
item.dc:creator: Ronnie Cheng

item.title: On the torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups of smooth quasi-projective varieties of rank up to seven
item.description: arXiv:2510.09026v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth quasi-projective variety. Assume that the (topological) fundamental group $\pi_1(X, x)$ is torsion-free nilpotent. We show that if the first Betti number $b_1(X) \le 3$, then $\pi_1(X, x)$ is isomorphic to either $\mathbb{Z}^n$ for $n = 1, 2, 3$, a lattice in the Heisenberg group $H_3(\mathbb{R})$ or $\mathbb{R} \times H_3(\mathbb{R})$. Moreover, we prove that $\pi_1(X, x)$ is abelian or $2$-step nilpotent if its rank is less than or equal to seven. More precisely, we determine the real nilpotent Lie groups in which torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups can be embedded as lattices for ranks up to six and seven, respectively. Our main results are a partial positive answer to a question on nilpotent (quasi-)K\"ahler groups posed by Aguilar and Campana.
item.dc:creator: Taito Shimoji

item.title: Hyperbolicity and fundamental groups of complex quasi-projective varieties (III): applications
item.description: arXiv:2512.20360v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is Part III of a series of three. We begin by introducing the notion of $h$-special varieties, which can be seen as varieties "chain-connected by the Zariski closures of entire curves." We prove that if $X$ is either a special smooth complex quasi-projective variety in the sense of Campana or an $h$-special variety, then for any linear representation $\rho:\pi_1(X)\to {\rm GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$, the image $\rho(\pi_1(X))$ is virtually nilpotent. We also provide examples showing that this result is sharp, leading to a revised form of Campana's abelianity conjecture for smooth quasi-projective varieties. In addition, we prove a structure theorem for quasi-projective varieties with big and semisimple representations of the fundamental groups, thereby addressing a conjecture by Koll\'ar in 1995. We also construct several examples of quasi-projective varieties that are special and $h$-special, highlighting certain atypical properties of the non-compact case in contrast with the projective setting.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Cadorel, Ya Deng, Katsutoshi Yamanoi

item.title: Toric schemes and integral models for Shimura varieties with $\Gamma_1(p)$-type level
item.description: arXiv:2602.23245v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a conjectural theory of $p$-integral models of Shimura varieties with level structure at $p$ given by a class of normal subgroups of parahoric subgroups with abelian quotient group. The role of the theory of local models is played in this context by a certain root stack over the local model for parahoric level. The construction of this root stack is based on the "divisor theorem" (a foundational fact about local models) and on the theory of toric varieties in this context, both of which are of independent interest. We prove our conjecture in the case of Shimura varieties of PEL type when the parahoric is an Iwahori (under some additional conditions).
item.dc:creator: Georgios Pappas, Michael Rapoport

item.title: Equivalued affine springer fibers in mixed characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2606.31083v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Witt-vector affine Springer fibers for tame equi-valued conjugacy classes in tamely ramified groups. Following the approach of Goresky-Kottwitz-MacPherson in the equal characteristic setting, we show that they admit pavings by iterations of perfections of affine space bundles whose base are smooth Hessenberg varieties. Along the way we revisit a version of the Chevalley restriction theorem for the dual of Lie algebras.
item.dc:creator: Jingren Chi

item.title: Geometric characterization of $p$-exceptional monomial GAPN functions
item.description: arXiv:2608.08969v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On finite fields of characteristic $p$, PN (perfect nonlinear) functions for odd $p$ and APN (almost perfect nonlinear) functions for even $p$ are well-known classes of highly nonlinear functions. GAPN (generalized almost perfect nonlinear) functions were introduced as a generalization of APN functions for even $p$ to all $p$. One of the main targets of studies on such highly nonlinear functions is their classification. While $p$-exceptional monomial PN and $2$-exceptional monomial APN functions have been classified, the corresponding problem for GAPN functions remains open. Here, a polynomial over $\mathbb{F}_p$ is called a $p$-exceptional PN (resp. APN, resp. GAPN) function if it is a PN (resp. APN, resp. GAPN) function on $\mathbb{F}_{p^n}$ for infinitely many positive integers $n$. In this paper, we give a geometric characterization of $p$-exceptional monomial GAPN functions. To this end, for a prime power $q$, we establish a geometric characterization of non-zero polynomials in $\mathbb{F}_{q}[x,y]$ having no absolutely irreducible factor defined over $\mathbb{F}_{q}$.
item.dc:creator: Masamichi Kuroda, Kentaro Mitsui

item.title: Torelli Theorem for moduli stacks of vector bundles on tame Deligne Mumford curves
item.description: arXiv:2609.29011v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a Torelli theorem for full moduli stacks of vector bundles of rank at least three with fixed determinant on a smooth, proper, geometrically connected, tame Deligne--Mumford curve of coarse genus at least two over an arbitrary field $k$. We also prove a Torelli theorem for the full moduli stack of vector bundles of rank at least three of fixed-degree under an explicit compatibility hypothesis. The method is intrinsic to the stack: faithful special-linear linearizations recover Picard stacks, and determinants of tangent complexes recover the canonical principal polarization. This is the first part in a series of two papers.
item.dc:creator: Soham Ghosh, Ting Gong, Max Lieblich

item.title: Euclidean Distance Optimization Within the Grassmannian
item.description: arXiv:2610.02018v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a subvariety of the Grassmannian and a data point, we seek to find a point on the subvariety minimizing the Euclidean distance to the data point. The number of complex critical points of this optimization problem is the Euclidean distance (ED) degree. We show that the ED discriminant of the whole Grassmannian, that is, the set of data points with a number of critical points different than the ED degree, is the discriminant of the characteristic polynomial of the data as a projection matrix. Another closely connected algebraic complexity measure for a subvariety in the Grassmannian is the Grassmann distance (GD) degree, which is the number of complex critical points of the distance optimization problem when the data point itself is in the Grassmannian. We give formulae for ED and GD degrees of geometrically meaningful subvarieties of the Grassmannian, namely, products of smaller Grassmannians, matroid realization varieties, and Schubert varieties.
item.dc:creator: Hannah Friedman, Serkan Ho\c{s}ten, Andrea Rosana

item.title: A Poincar\'e-Lefschetz Theorem for Cellular Cosheaves and an Application to the Tropical Homology of Orbifold Toric Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2308.08548v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We begin by presenting a version of the Poincar\'e-Lefschetz theorem for certain cellular cosheaves on a particular subdivision of a CW-complex K. To that end we construct a cellular sheaf on K whose cohomology with compact support is isomorphic to the homology of the initial cosheaf. Thereafter we use the first result to generalise the tropical version of the Lefschetz Hyperplane Section Theorem to some singular tropical toric varieties and singular tropical hypersurfaces.
item.dc:creator: Jules Chenal

item.title: On properness of moduli stacks of $D^{\times}$-shtukas over ramified legs
item.description: arXiv:2505.18977v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a maximal order $\mathcal{D}$ of a central division algebra $D$ over a global function field $F$, we prove an explicit necessary and sufficient condition for moduli stacks of $\mathcal{D}^\times$-shtukas to be proper over a finite field (modulo a suitable central action) in terms of the local invariants of $D$ and bounds. Our result extends E. Lau's criterion (Duke Math. J. 140 (2007)) for properness of the leg morphism (or characteristic morphism) away from the ramification locus of $D$ to allow legs at ramified places. We also establish non-emptiness of Newton and Kottwitz-Rapoport strata for moduli stacks of $\mathcal{B}^\times$-shtukas, where $\mathcal{B}$ is a maximal order of a central simple algebra over $F$.
item.dc:creator: Yong-Gyu Choi, Wansu Kim, Junyeong Park

item.title: Counting symmetric unimodular triangulations
item.description: arXiv:2605.14150v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The objects of study are triangulations of the dilated standard triangle in the plane. Motivated by work on T-curves (Geiselmann et al., 2026), the focus lies on unimodular triangulations with a fixed symmetry axis. Lower and upper bounds are given, in combination with full enumerations of a few small cases.
item.dc:creator: Kamillo Ferry, Michael Joswig, J\"org Rambau

item.title: The arithmetic of critical values II: critical elliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2608.29836v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this second chapter of the $\textit{Arithmetic of critical values}$ series (ACV), we study certain double covers $E_f\to\mathbb{P}^1$ whose branch locus coincides with that of a quartic polynomial $f$. We give a direct proof of the fact, already shown non-constructively in ACV I, that the elliptic curves $E_f$ admit a $3$-isogeny. Our methods are Galois-theoretic, and lead us to a thorough analysis of the Galois closure of $f:\mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{P}^1$. We exploit its rich geometry to prove a Selmer companionship theorem for the family $E_f$, allowing us to exhibit elements in certain Tate-Shafarevich groups which are visible in an abelian surface. We also give some dynamical and Diophantine applications of our constructions, as well as new examples of Jacobians isogenous to a power of an elliptic curve.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Naccarato

item.title: Equivariant Chow functions and Wonderful Models in type A and B
item.description: arXiv:2610.03138v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a general inversion formula in the equivariant incidence algebras of geometric lattices that relates the equivariant Chow function with the equivariant super-reduced characteristic function. We apply this result to the case of minimal wonderful models for hyperplane arrangements associated to root systems, with the natural action of the corresponding Weyl group. Applying this formula to type $A$ (i.e. the partition lattices), we recover Getzler's compositional identity in type $A$. In type $B$ (i.e. the signed partition lattice), we recover Henderson's result, expressing the equivariant Chow generating series in terms of the same series in type $A$ and the equivariant characteristic generating series of type $B$. Moreover, we obtain a new compositional identity for the equivariant Chow generating series.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Pagaria, Tommaso Scognamiglio

item.title: Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane, with a proof formalized in Lean
item.description: arXiv:2610.13100v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to similarity. This settles Smale's sixth problem for five bodies in the plane. Albouy and Kaloshin proved it for masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two. We follow their method. Infinitely many central configurations would give an algebraic curve of complex solutions. At the places at infinity of the curve the valuations of the mutual distances must balance. We determine the possible valuation vectors at all positive masses, together with the mass conditions under which each can occur. We treat limits in which four bodies form a cluster of zero potential energy by expanding the potential, which is constant along the curve, at a place. This excludes, at every positive mass, one of the two diagrams in which such clusters occur, and part of the other. The same expansion excludes one further diagram at every positive mass. What remains is an exact analysis, by computer algebra, of the sets of mass conditions that can hold together at positive masses. Exact rational certificates show that the balance fails under each of them, except on a few one-parameter families of masses, which we treat separately. On the rays through $(1,4,4,4,4)$ and $(1,1,4,4,4)$ the certificates do not apply. On the first ray they cannot apply: there the complex equations have a continuum of solutions, as Albouy and Kaloshin observed. On these rays we count the real central configurations: there are 306 and 294 up to orientation-preserving similarity. The certificates, the programs that check them and a proof of the theorem in the Lean proof assistant are available.
item.dc:creator: Tejasvi Singh Tomar

item.title: An introduction to algebraic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.21926v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We review the theory of abelian varieties and, more generally, algebraic groups, with a view toward arithmetic applications. We discuss their models over the rings of integers of number fields, their reductions modulo primes, their torsion points (together with their natural Galois action), and the interplay of these notions through characteristic polynomials of Frobenius.
item.dc:creator: Davide Lombardo
